title: Canva Slide Translator — Setup Guide
author: Han
course: A setup guide for the Canva slide translator being trialled in classes taught by {author} at iU University. Currently supports Canva viewing links only.
intro: Read Japanese slides in a separate panel in your chosen language. The panel updates when you change slides. You can also view the Japanese original. Numbers and text colors are preserved where available.
update: Already installed? Go to step 04, replace all the existing script code, save, and reload Canva.
step1: Use Google Chrome 138 or later on a computer. Updating to the latest version is usually sufficient.
The translation feature does not support smartphones. Device or administrator settings may also restrict access.
step2: In the Chrome Web Store, select “Add to Chrome”, then “Add extension”. If already installed, continue to the next step.
step3: Enter the address above in Chrome’s address bar.
step4Intro: To update, open your existing script and replace all its code instead of creating another script.
step4: Open Tampermonkey from Chrome’s extensions menu at the top right, then select “Create a new script”.
Select and delete all the default code in the editor.
Paste the code and save with ⌘+S (Mac) or Ctrl+S (Windows).
manualCopy: Click the code field. Use ⌘+A then ⌘+C (Mac), or Ctrl+A then Ctrl+C (Windows).
enabled: After saving, check that the script below is enabled in the dashboard. Disable any older Canva translation scripts.
step5: Open the shared viewing link for your slides in Chrome. Reload if it is already open.
A “Slide translator” panel appears. The tool does not run in Canva’s editor.
step6: Choose the language you want to read, such as English, in the panel.
Click “{start}”. For Japanese, choose 日本語 and click “{original}” (show original).
Once text appears, browse by changing slides. The panel updates automatically.
downloadNote: The first translation may take time to download language data. Viewing the Japanese original needs no language download.
restartNote: After reloading or changing the text language, click the start button again.
usageIntro: Button names below assume the slide language matches this guide and button translation is on. Turning it off shows buttons in Japanese.
rows: Drag near the title at the top.
Drag the “↙” corner at the bottom left.
Click “{retry}”. For the Japanese original, use “{refresh}” (refresh display).
Select another language and click the start button.
Toggle “{translateUi}”. On: same language as the text. Off: Japanese. The text language stays the same.
Choose 日本語 and click “{original}” (show original).
Use ＋ or − under Text size. The range is 12–32 px; the default is 17 px. Your choice is saved when browser storage is available.
usageNotes: Routine hints are hidden. Status appears only during processing, while waiting for text, or on errors.
Button language is shared across slides in this browser. Reading order is saved per slide; unset slides use row order.

Reselect reading order after editing slide text. Slides in the same design with indistinguishable text and links share a setting. If storage is restricted, settings last until reload. Hover over the selector or checkbox for storage details.
help: Check the script and “Allow user scripts” are enabled, confirm you opened a viewing link, then reload Canva.
This is normal. Choose a language and click the start button.
Read the displayed error. Chrome or administrator settings may restrict built-in translation.
Text inside images is excluded. Standard lists retain numbers, symbols and nested indentation, but custom numbering or slide structures may not be readable. Numbers are not translated.
Set “{pageOrder}” to “{orderColumns}”. Row order remains if no clear column boundary can be found.
Different colors are translated separately, which can affect phrasing. A background may be added behind light text.
Running translation again may produce the same result.
footer: Updated 2 October 2026 · Included code v2.8.0. This trial may not work with every slide structure or environment.
